title: Black Streaks on Houston Shingles
description: Dark streaks on Houston asphalt shingles are usually algae from shade and humidity. A pressure washer takes the granules off with the stain.
html:
The north slope looks dirty. The streaks run downhill, darker where the oak shades the roof, lighter where the afternoon sun hits. That pattern is algae, the kind that thrives in Gulf humidity. It is not the same problem as granules in the gutter, and washing it like a driveway shortens the roof.

Algae stains. Granules leave.

The dark organism on asphalt shingles is a blue-green alga that reads black once it dries. It feeds on the limestone filler in the shingle. Shade, a tree that drips, and a slope that stays damp give it a head start. It is ugly. It is not, by itself, a leak, and it does not mean the roof has failed.

Granule loss is the opposite clue. Bald spots, grit in the gutter, and asphalt showing through are wear. We wrote that up separately in granules in the gutter. If you have both, the streaks are cosmetic and the bald spots are the thing to measure. Do not let a cleaning quote turn into a replacement, and do not let a replacement quote ignore a slope that is actually worn out.

What not to spray

A pressure washer cuts the granules off. The roof looks clean for a month and older for the next ten years. Bleach mixes sold for siding can run into the beds and stain metal. If the streaks bother you, a soft wash from someone who roofs, or at least someone who will stay off a steep slope, is the careful version. Zinc strips near the ridge can slow the streaks on a new roof. They do not erase ten years of shade, and they do not belong on every system.

We will not sell a new asphalt roof because the north side is dark. We will tell you if the shingles under the streaks are still sealed and granulated. If you want the streaks read in person, request a free inspection or call (281) 541-0027.
